newsitem.title: USA: Bio-Tech General seen growing - report.
newsitem.headline: Bio-Tech General seen growing - report.

text.p: Some investors and analysts are bullish on Bio-Technology General Corp even though its stock has been hit by profit-taking recently, according to a column in the latest issue of Business Week magazine.
The "Inside Wall Street" column quoted investors and analysts as saying they were optimistic about an improvement in the drug company's earnings.
It said the company went into the black in 1995 when it launched its first major product, Oxandrin, which is used to treat involuntary weight loss brought on by cancer, AIDS or severe trauma.

Merrill Lynch analyst Paul Woodhouse "projects sales of Oxandrin of $39 million in 1997 and $60 million next year," it said, adding that Woodhouse saw Oxandrin as the main growth engine for the company for the next two years.
On Thursday, its stock closed at 13-3/4 on the Nasdaq stock market. The column said the stock had risen to 17-3/4 on February 20 from five on April 10, 1996.
